newsitem.title: CANADA: Renaissance falls on lower profit picture.
newsitem.headline: Renaissance falls on lower profit picture.

text.p: Shares of Renaissance Energy Ltd sank in busy volume in early Wednesday trade after the company projected lower profits in 1997 and first-quarter results came in below expectations, analysts said.
Renaissance, Canada's busiest oil and gas driller, was off 1.30 to 38.40 on volume of 739,175 shares.

Renaissance Chief Executive Clayton Woitas told shareholders at the firm's annual meeting on Tuesday that high oil and gas prices played a big role in last year's strong earnings and commodity markets were expected to remain weaker this year.
He said the company was projected to post 1997 earnings of C$140 million, down from C$180 million last year.
Peter Linder, analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy, said also that the company's first-quarter cash flow per share did not live up to his expectations of C$1.45.
The company posted cash flow of C$1.27 per share, up from C$1.12 in the year earlier period.
Linder said he did not expect Renaissance's higher operating costs and royalty rate for the first three months of 1997.
"I want to stress they're still very low compared to its peers, but they did take a big jump," he said.
The company reported royalty rate increases of 25 percent for oil production and 89 percent for natural gas production in the period.
Operating costs rose by three percent for oil production and 23 percent for gas production, the company said.
